rules.title: California Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations for housing
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but face strict limits on what is sought and how it is used. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record, and policies that consider arrests without convictions, are prohibited.
citation_aliases: Civil Rights Council (formerly Fair Employment and Housing Council) criminal history regulations
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.effective_date_note: Document says regulations took effect Jan. 1, 2020. The regulation section cite is not stated in the document.
rules.key_value: no blanket bans on criminal records; no consideration of arrests without convictions
rules.conflict_note: The regulation section number is not given in the document and is inferred.

rules.title: FEHA source-of-income protection for housing subsidies (SB 329)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to participate in government housing subsidy programs such as Section 8. 'No Section 8' policies are unlawful.
rules.quoted_span: state law prohibits landlords from refusing to participate in such programs.
rules.key_value: ban on refusing Section 8 / housing subsidy programs

rules.title: FEHA credit history limit for subsidy holders (SB 267)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot use the credit history of an applicant with a government rental subsidy without offering the option to give alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.quoted_span: last year’s SB 267 amended FEHA to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process
rules.effective_date_note: The document gives no effective date, only 'last year'.
rules.key_value: must offer alternative evidence of ability to pay for subsidy holders

parsed.doc_summary: California Apartment Association compliance reminder on state fair housing limits for tenant screening. It covers the Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations, SB 329 source-of-income protections for Section 8 and similar subsidies, and SB 267 limits on credit history use for subsidy holders.
